risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- MD&A states macroeconomic conditions 'remain highly volatile, influencing commodities, food inflation, and consumption patterns' — the food division's input cost and offtake both sit on that swing.
- Management explicitly flags that 'energy-driven inflation may temporarily impact discretionary consumption', even while maintaining India's structural almond demand is strong and resilient. Almonds are a discretionary food purchase, so demand is the first line to compress in an inflation shock.
- Listed by management as a ripple effect of global instability, 'persistent INR volatility despite RBI intervention' — relevant to a food business whose product is substantially import-linked and whose related-party purchases are from an overseas counterparty.
- Named by management among the effects of global instability being felt in India; feeds directly into the inflation channel management links to consumption.
- Management names a sharp increase in air freight, road transport and insurance costs — a direct margin pressure on a trading-led food division that carries no manufacturing base to absorb it.
- MD&A records that the RBI has projected GDP growth to moderate to 6.6% in FY 2026-27 from 7.7% in FY 2025-26 because of downside risks from the West Asia crisis, and describes ongoing conflicts as being in 'a phase of fragile calm' with underlying tensions unresolved.
- The Board's risk-management policy paragraph names the key risks facing the business as 'significant weakening in demand from core-end markets, inflation uncertainties and any adverse regulatory developments'. The same paragraph records that a risk analysis and assessment was conducted during the year and 'no major risks were noticed', so this is the Board's stated risk universe rather than a live flag.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue operating the two existing divisions — food and finance — as the Company's two reportable segments under Ind AS-108, with no stated pivot, new vertical or restructuring.
- Position the finance division as a private-finance provider competing on speed, flexibility and customised terms rather than on the terms conventional banking offers.
- Stay asset-light and unlevered by deposits: no subsidiaries, joint ventures or associates; no public deposits accepted; no fresh capital infusion during the year.
